ai_show_review.summary: Stunning Scarlet>Fire, soaring Fire on the Mountain and tight jams
ai_show_review.blurb: The Montego Bay set shines with a blistering Scarlet Begonias → Fire on the Mountain transition at sunrise and an inspired Fire on the Mountain later in the night. Jerry’s crystal‑clear tone, Brent’s lush organ textures, and the twin‑drum thunder keep the energy high throughout a compact yet potent performance.
ai_show_review.review: What unfolds at the Bob Marley Performing Arts Center is a sun‑kissed snapshot of the Dead in late‑’82, delivering one of the most memorable Scarlet Begonias → Fire on the Mountain moments of the era. The first set rolls smoothly through Sugaree and Althea before giving way to a second half that bursts into Samson & Delilah and then launches into an electrified Scarlet jam that seamlessly morphs into a soaring Fire on the Mountain as the Caribbean dawn breaks. Jerry’s guitar sings with pristine clarity, his vocals rise above the mix, and Brent’s Hammond organ adds a rich, rippling backdrop that lifts the improvisations. Phil pushes forward with funk‑infused bass lines that lock tightly with Mickey and Billy's thunderous, almost tribal drum segment, while Bob provides steady rhythm work and joins in vocal harmonies on Not Fade Away. Though a few tracks (Althea → Let It Grow) feel less inspired, the overall flow is high‑energy, cohesive, and perfectly captures the festival vibe of Montego Bay.

best_recording.reason: Pristine soundboard capture with clear, crisp mix; superior fidelity despite minor speed/pitch quirks makes it the definitive listening source

key_highlights: Magical Scarlet Begonias → Fire on the Mountain transition at sunrise
Soaring Fire on the Mountain later in the set showcases Jerry’s shredding solo
Tight, tribal drum segment by Mickey and Billy adds a powerful rhythmic centerpiece
Brent’s Hammond organ and synth textures provide lush back‑drops throughout

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia delivers crystal‑clear tone and soaring leads, especially on the Scarlet>Fire sequence and Fire on the Mountain; vocals are strong overall with only a brief dip on Althea.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh’s bass steps forward with funkier lines that drive the jams, notably supporting Jerry during the Scarlet jam and providing a solid foundation throughout.
band_performance.Bob: Weir offers steady rhythm guitar work and adds vocal harmonies on Not Fade Away; his presence keeps the band grounded despite occasional missed growls on Throwing Stones.
band_performance.Brent: Mydland’s Hammond organ is described as lush and “cripping,” while his synth work adds aggressive texture to the climax, enhancing both ballads and high‑energy jams.
band_performance.Mickey: Hart delivers tight, powerful drumming; his interplay with Billy creates an almost tribal 5‑minute drum segment that elevates the second set.
band_performance.Billy: Kreutzmann’s drums are crisp and forceful, matching Mickey’s intensity and providing a solid rhythmic backbone throughout the show.
